findings.title: Migration crashes when no site setting matches a category
findings.body: The lookup `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes the first row of the result. When `embed_category` is unset, or its value matches no category name, the result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. Most installs never set embed_category, so this migration will fail for them and block the upgrade. The lookup needs a nil/empty check with a fallback to uncategorized.

findings.title: Host values interpolated into SQL unescaped
findings.body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated directly into an INSERT string: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration. Parameter binding or quoting via the connection (`connection.quote`) should be used.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on missing host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If the request omits `embeddable_host[host]`, `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is nil and `host` is nil, so `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError. The controller then returns a 500 rather than a validation error. A nil guard is needed, and the validator should report a blank host.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, and there is no unique index. `record_for_host` uses `.first` on `lower(host) = ?`, so when duplicates exist, the category a topic gets (via TopicEmbed.import) and the allow/deny decision are arbitrary. The migration also inserts whatever the old setting contained, so duplicates are plausible. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and a unique index on lower(host).

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side
findings.body: The query compares `lower(host)` against the raw `uri.host`, which is not downcased. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com/page) never matches a stored host, so the embed is rejected. The argument should be downcased before comparing.

findings.title: update and destroy crash on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` can return nil. `save_host(host)` then raises on `host.host =` and `destroy` raises on `host.destroy`. The client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` (which raises RecordNotFound, rendered as 404) or check for nil.

findings.title: PUT /customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: The `update` action only re-renders the current embedding and never reads params or saves anything. The client `saveChanges` action calls `update({})`, so any submitted change is silently discarded while the response looks like a successful save. Either implement the update or remove the route and client action.

findings.title: saveChanges calls update with an empty payload
findings.body: `this.get('embedding').update({})` sends no data, and the backing PUT endpoint does nothing. This action is dead or misleading and does not persist the host list. It should be removed or wired to something that saves.

findings.title: Fabricator contents swapped between files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now contains only the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The file names no longer match their contents, which will mislead maintainers looking for category fabricators.

findings.title: Controller specs only test inheritance
findings.body: The spec only asserts that the controller subclasses AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, or destroy, staff-only access, the blank-category fallback to uncategorized, or validation failure responses. The same applies to embedding_controller_spec.rb, which would not have caught the no-op update.

findings.title: No test for duplicate hosts, nil host, or mixed-case lookup
findings.body: The model spec covers trimming and basic matching but not the edge cases the code is sensitive to: duplicate hosts, a missing host param (nil crash), or a mixed-case host or referer. The describe label 'allows_embeddable_host' is also a leftover from the removed SiteSetting method.

findings.title: Migration has no test and an irreversible change
findings.body: The migration moves data from site settings into a new table and then deletes the old settings. It has no spec, and the `change` method cannot be reversed, since the DELETE has no inverse. Rolling back loses the embed configuration.
